claims.claim: In-batch negatives are a training trick for DPR.
Passages in the same mini-batch are reused as negatives.
Negatives are used for other questions in the batch.
A batch contains B questions and relevant passages.
The model computes a B x B similarity matrix.
The similarity matrix is S = Q P^T.
Diagonal entries pair a question with its true passage.
Off-diagonal entries treat other passages as negatives.
Each batch yields B^2 question-passage pairs.
This provides many negative examples without extra sampling.
This approach increases the number of training pairs.
Accuracy improves as batch size grows.
